==Problem==
Mike cycled <imath>15</imath> laps in <imath>57</imath> minutes. Assume he cycled at a constant speed throughout. Approximately how many laps did he complete in the first <imath>27</imath> minutes?

<imath>\textbf{(A) } 5 \qquad\textbf{(B) } 7 \qquad\textbf{(C) } 9 \qquad\textbf{(D) } 11 \qquad\textbf{(E) } 13</imath>

== Solution 1== 

Mike's speed is <imath>\frac{15}{57}=\frac{5}{19}</imath> laps per minute.

In the first <imath>27</imath> minutes, he completed approximately <imath>\frac{5}{19}\cdot27\approx\frac{1}{4}\cdot28=\boxed{\textbf{(B) } 7}</imath> laps.

~MRENTHUSIASM

== Solution 2==

Mike runs <imath>1</imath> lap in <imath>\frac{57}{15}=\frac{19}{5}</imath> minutes. So, in <imath>27</imath> minutes, Mike ran about <imath>\frac{27}{\frac{19}{5}} \approx \boxed{\textbf{(B) }7}</imath> laps.

~MrThinker

== Solution 3== 
Mike's rate is <cmath>\frac{15}{57}=\frac{x}{27},</cmath> where <imath>x</imath> is the number of laps he can complete in <imath>27</imath> minutes. 
If you cross multiply, <imath>57x = 405</imath>. 

So, <imath>x = \frac{405}{57} \approx \boxed{\textbf{(B) }7}</imath>. 

~Shiloh000

== Solution 4 (Quick Estimate) == 
Note that <imath>27</imath> minutes is a little bit less than half of <imath>57</imath> minutes. Mike will therefore run a little bit less than <imath>15/2=7.5</imath> laps, which is about <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(B) }7}</imath>. 

~UltimateDL

== Solution 5 (Approximation)==
Note that <imath>57</imath> minutes is almost equal to <imath>1</imath> hour. Running <imath>15</imath> laps in <imath>1</imath> hour is running approximately <imath>1</imath> lap every <imath>4</imath> minutes. This means that in <imath>27</imath> minutes, Mike will run approximately <imath>\frac{27}{4}</imath> laps. This is very close to <imath>\frac{28}{4} = \boxed{\textbf{(B) }7}</imath>.

== Solution 6 (Dimensional Analysis)==
<cmath> \frac{15 \text{ laps}}{57 \text{ minutes}} \cdot 27 \text{ minutes} = \frac{135}{19} \text{ laps} \approx \boxed{\textbf{(B) }7} \text{ laps}</cmath>
~Blosp
